rules: Every fumble, dropped tool, wrong step or spark adds noise. When the meter fills, the infected arrive and the game ends early (counts as a fail).

How fast infected arrive scales with the local infectious share from the SEIR curve: arrival time = base time / (1 + 10 x infectious share) (fictional rule). Manhattan on Day 4 is far less forgiving than Teton County.
Drag and hold actions lag and shake more in the cold.
Control lag = 1 + 0.02 x degrees below 32°F, using the stop's real NOAA January normal (fictional rule on real data).
Each game has a real-world correct order. Steps done out of order trigger the consequence listed for that game.
Procedures follow standard guidance (tire changing, jump-starting, first aid, cold injuries, water safety, carbon monoxide).
EASY shows a checklist and a long timer; NORMAL hides the checklist; HARD hides it, shortens the timer and adds a second problem.
Same HARD/NORMAL/EASY roll rules as the original eight games.
A mini game does not repeat in one playthrough. Story-linked games play when their scene calls for them; any not yet played join the random roll pool.
The original eight games stay in the roll pool, so 18 games in total.
games: Change a Flat in the Dark
Drag tools on a close-up of the wheel; hold the flashlight steady with the other hand (mouse button or second finger).

1. Wedge the wheel opposite the flat. 2. Loosen lug nuts a half turn while the tire is on the ground. 3. Jack at the frame point. 4. Remove nuts, swap the tire. 5. Hand-tighten, lower, then tighten in a star pattern.
Jacking before loosening: the wheel spins (time, noise). Wrong jack point: the car drops (injury). Dropped lug nut: search the snow (noise).
Cold hands (NOAA normal); noise meter (local infection).
EASY 120 s, checklist | NORMAL 90 s | HARD 70 s, one lug nut is seized
Keep your vehicle; no time lost
Vehicle lost OR 3 h delay; -10 health if the car drops
Jump-Start a Dead Battery
Drag cable clamps onto battery terminals, then hold to crank and watch the dash lights.

1. Red clamp on the dead battery (+). 2. Red on the good battery (+). 3. Black on the good battery (-). 4. Black on bare metal away from the dead battery. 5. Run the good car, then crank. Remove in reverse order.
Wrong order or touching clamps: sparks (injury -8, big noise). Cranking too long: battery drains, start over.
Cold hands; cold batteries need more cranking attempts below 20°F (NOAA normal).
EASY labeled terminals | NORMAL unlabeled | HARD dirty terminals to scrape first
Vehicle starts; +2 h saved
Stranded: plays the On Foot fallback
Treat a Wound
Open a first-aid kit and drag items onto the wound; hold pressure with a press-and-hold gauge.
1. Gloves. 2. Firm direct pressure until bleeding slows (hold the gauge in the green). 3. Rinse with clean water. 4. Look closely: bite marks or not. 5. Bandage and note the time.
Too little pressure: bleeding continues (-5 health per 10 s). Alcohol in a deep wound: stings (noise). Skip the look: a bite stays hidden.
Infection system: a correct check tells you whether you were bitten, so treatment can start before symptoms (rabies-style rule).
EASY 90 s, kit labeled | NORMAL 60 s | HARD 45 s, two wounds
+10 health; learn your true infection status
-10 health; infection status stays hidden
Cold Emergency Triage
Check a shivering companion (tap to inspect speech, skin, fingers), then drag actions into order.
1. Out of the wind. 2. Remove wet clothes. 3. Dry layers and a sleeping bag. 4. Warm sweet drink if alert. 5. Frostbite: rewarm in warm, not hot, water; don't rub.
Rubbing frostbite or using hot water: tissue damage (-10 health). Skipping wet clothes: condition worsens on the timer.
Difficulty (how fast the companion worsens) uses the stop's real NOAA January normal.
EASY 120 s, signs labeled | NORMAL 90 s | HARD 60 s, companion also has frostbite
Companion saved; +10 health
Companion lost or -15 health
Make Water Safe
Pick a water source, pour it through a cloth filter, light the stove, and stop the boil timer at the right moment (or count bleach drops from the label chart).
1. Choose the clearest source. 2. Filter through cloth. 3. Rolling boil 1 minute, or 3 minutes above 6,500 ft (CDC guidance). 4. Cool and store covered.
Boil too short: sick later (-15 health over 12 h). Boil far too long: stove fuel wasted (-1 gal fuel). Wrong source: worse odds.
Elevation from the real NOAA station: Laramie (about 7,270 ft), Rock Springs (about 6,740 ft), Dillon (about 9,070 ft) need the longer boil.
EASY elevation shown | NORMAL you must check the map | HARD the stove sputters
+30 water
-15 health over the next 12 h
Siphon Fuel
Feed a hose into the tank, squeeze a pump bulb in rhythm, and keep the gas can below the tank.
1. Hose past the anti-rollover valve (wiggle to feel it). 2. Can on the ground, below the tank. 3. Pump the bulb until flow starts. 4. Stop before the can overflows.
Can held above the tank: no flow. Over-pumping: spill (fire risk, injury -8, noise). Forcing the hose: it jams.
Noise meter uses local infection; cold hands slow the pump rhythm.
EASY 90 s | NORMAL 70 s | HARD 50 s, tank half empty
+5 to +10 gal fuel (by how well you did)
No fuel; possible -8 health
Put On Tire Chains
Drape a chain over the tire, connect hooks on the inside then the outside, then tighten and drive a few feet to recheck.
1. Lay the chain flat, no twists. 2. Drape over the tire. 3. Hook the inside first. 4. Hook the outside. 5. Tighten, drive 10 ft, retighten.
Twisted chain or loose hooks: it snaps on the climb (injury -10, time). Skipping the recheck: loosens halfway.
Cold hands; plays on the snowy mountain stops (NOAA snowfall).
EASY 120 s | NORMAL 90 s | HARD 60 s, both tires
Mountain crossing at low risk
Slide on the grade: -15 health or a 3 h delay
Navigate by Map and Compass
A paper road map of the real counties on your route. Rotate the compass, read a bearing, and trace a detour while watching the odometer.
1. Orient the map to north. 2. Mark where you are. 3. Pick roads that avoid the closure. 4. Follow the bearing; check landmarks every few miles.
Wrong bearing: extra miles and fuel. Ignoring landmarks: a dead end.
Real county names and road distances (OpenStreetMap/OSRM) on the map.
EASY landmarks marked | NORMAL some marked | HARD night, flashlight only
Shortcut: -3 h travel
+40 miles and fuel used
Find the Emergency Broadcast
Turn a radio dial through static, fine-tune by ear (the signal clears as you get close), and type the key facts you hear.
1. Scan the NOAA Weather Radio band (162.400-162.550 MHz). 2. Fine-tune until the static clears. 3. Note closures, safe-zone hours, and the weather.
Moving too fast: you miss the message. Wrong notes: you act on bad info.
Real NOAA Weather Radio frequencies; the message names real towns and road closures on your route.
EASY strong signal | NORMAL weak signal | HARD signal drifts
Route info: a shortcut or warning (acts like an ally flag)
No info
Snowed In: Carbon Monoxide
Your car is buried. Dig around the car, check the tailpipe, crack a window, then run the heater on a timer.
1. Clear the tailpipe completely. 2. Crack a window on the downwind side. 3. Run the engine about 10 minutes an hour. 4. Stay awake for the timer.
Running the engine with a blocked tailpipe: the screen blurs and health drains until you fix it. Never running it: cold damage.
Snow depth uses the stop's real NOAA January snowfall.
EASY reminders shown | NORMAL none | HARD fuel low, so every minute of heat costs fuel
A safe night: +10 health
-15 health (CO) or -10 health (cold)
